trustworthy.note: Verified = same service as the incident. Nothing in the data states a deployment caused its incident.

insufficient_evidence.logs: All 4 non-INFO messages appear on all 7 services; no incident has a matching log on its own service within 24h of its deployment. Logs cannot corroborate any incident.
insufficient_evidence.incident_timestamps: Incidents have no start/end timestamps, so no temporal relationship to a deployment can be established.

human_input_needed: Correct deployment_id (or 'none') for the 8 quarantined incidents
Whether the logs are synthetic placeholders or should be regenerated per service
Any real cross-service dependencies, with a source document

observations: incident and deployment IDs are sequential (INC-001..INC-020, DEP-101..DEP-120); there is one deployment per day from 2026-05-02 to 2026-05-21 and each is 3 minutes later in the day than the previous one (10:03, 10:06, ... 10:57, then 10:00)
each of the 4 non-INFO log messages appears on all 7 services
provenance.interpretation: These patterns are typical of generated placeholder data, but nothing in the repository states whether the records are synthetic or real. The application therefore treats provenance as unconfirmed: strict seeding refuses it and /health reports it.
provenance.needs_human_input: Data owner to set status to 'synthetic' or 'real' (with a source).
